Class Panel.Builder

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.Panel.Builder
Enclosing class:
Panel
public static final class Panel.Builder extends Object
Builds a Panel. Defaults: visible, PanelStyle.RAISED, no placement, and no toggle key unless toggleKey(int) is called.

    • in

      public Panel.Builder in(ModeScope scope, Placement placement)
      Where the panel goes in scope (7.4.0): ModeScope.SURVIVAL, ModeScope.CREATIVE or ModeScope.BOTH, once each. Each frame the panel takes the current mode's placement, else its BOTH one; with neither it doesn't show in that mode, and with no player only BOTH applies. The two modes' placements can be anything: a screen region in one, beside an anchor in the other. 
      Panel.builder("mymod:sort")
        .in(ModeScope.SURVIVAL, Placement.screen(PanelPosition.region(OutsideRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP)))
        .in(ModeScope.CREATIVE, Placement.at(MY_ANCHOR, 0, -18))
        .add(sortButton)
        .build();
      A panel with no placement at all (a nested panel, a dialog, a standalone screen's default stack) is BOTH by nature.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when scope already has a placement, or with position(PanelPosition)

    • position

      @Deprecated(since="7.4.0", forRemoval=true) public Panel.Builder position(PanelPosition position)
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Replaced in 7.4.0 by in(ModeScope, Placement), which picks the mode scope; removed in 8.0.0. in(ModeScope.BOTH, Placement.screen(position)) is this call.
      Sets where the panel sits in both modes; every host reads this. Unplaced by default: adapters and the HUD reject an unplaced panel; MKScreen and CustomContainerMenu make the first unplaced panel their main() and stack later ones below it.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - with in(ModeScope, Placement)

    • fixed

      public Panel.Builder fixed()
      The player can't move this panel (7.4.0): it stays where its placements put it. Without it a player may move the panel with MenuKit's edit mode (the "Move panels" key), and the place they put it is kept under the panel's id, for both modes or one. Background panels, overlays, popovers and a screen's main panel are never movable, with or without this.

    • popover

      public Panel.Builder popover()
      Makes the panel a popover: something that pops up over the screen while it is shown (a row of pockets over a hovered hotbar slot, a flyout from a button). It draws above every ordinary panel on the screen, whichever host holds it or them (a container screen's adapters, an anchor's, a standalone screen's own) and whichever registered first, and below a modal and its dim. Input follows the picture: a click, the wheel, hover or a tooltip over a popover reach it, never a panel drawn under it. Its own slots stay live under it as any panel's do.

      Where it sits is still its position(PanelPosition); only its layer changes. Among popovers, and among ordinary panels, the sorted order (priority, then mod, then registration) still decides which is on top. Default: an ordinary panel.

    • background

      public Panel.Builder background()
      Makes the panel part of the screen's background (7.4.0): it draws right where the screen draws its own image, after the screen's dim, so everything else on the screen draws over it: vanilla's labels and slots, other mods' widgets and buttons, every other panel, tooltips. It never interferes with anything drawn over it:
      • It claims nothing (the claim rule, docs/concepts.md "Claims"): what lies over it stays live, including another mod's widget anywhere on it.
      • Its elements get input last: a click once the screen's own widgets (and so every other mod's) and every panel above have declined it, and never on a slot it shows, which is vanilla's to click; the wheel once the screen and every other handler have declined it.
      • Its slots draw with it, right after its elements, over the panel and clipped to what it shows of them, and so under the screen's widgets: another mod's button over one of its slots covers the item. Each goes through the screen's own extractSlot, so every mod's per-slot hook still marks it, and its hover highlight and tooltip are vanilla's.
      The container region's two panels are background panels. Not with popover(): a panel is above everything or below it.
